svg.text: Walkthrough: C = A × B on a 2×2 weight-stationary array
a[m][k]: m = which C-row we're building, k = which grid row it enters
PE(k,n) holds b[k][n]. Grid column n produces C[·][n].
What enters grid row k each cycle (skew = k cycles)
grid row 0: 1 3 – – ← column 0 of A: a[0][0], a[1][0]
grid row 1: – 2 4 – ← column 1 of A, one cycle late
Legend: blue = A value moving right black = partial sum moving down red = finished C element
a[0][0]=1 enters row 0. PE(0,0) multiplies by its weight 5 → partial sum 5 (start of C[0][0]). Row 1 waits.
1 slid right to PE(0,1) → 6 (start of C[0][1]). New a[1][0]=3 enters row 0 → 15 (start of C[1][0]). a[0][1]=2 enters row 1 and meets the 5 from above: 5+2·7 = 19 = C[0][0] DONE.
3 slid right → 18 (start C[1][1]). 2 slid right, meets 6: 6+2·8 = 22 = C[0][1]. a[1][1]=4 enters row 1, meets 15: 15+4·7 = 43 = C[1][0]. Bottom of column 0 outputs 19.
4 slid right, meets 18: 18+4·8 = 50 = C[1][1]. Column 0 outputs 43, column 1 outputs 22 (a cycle behind: that's the deskew). Cycle 5 would output 50.
→ Right (blue): A values. They are only being REUSED — a[m][k] is needed by every column n, so it slides across all of them. No maths happens along this direction.
↓ Down (black): the partial sum. Each PE adds its own product to what came from above. Going down one row = adding the next k term. This IS the accumulation.
× Inside each PE: exactly one multiply (a × its stored b) and one add (+ the incoming partial sum) per clock. Nothing else.
Skew: a[m][1] enters row 1 one cycle after a[m][0] enters row 0, so it arrives just as the partial sum from row 0 drops down. Wrong timing = adds the wrong C-row's sum.
Output: bottom of grid column n emits C[0][n], C[1][n], C[2][n]… one per clock. Column 1 is one cycle behind column 0; the deskew registers line them up.
Steady state for 8×8: every clock, one new row of A enters (8 values), all 64 PEs work, one finished row of C leaves. 64 MACs per clock from 8 inputs.
For K > 8 (real matrices): the C values that exit are only partial. They go into the C buffer and the next K-tile's results are added to them (read-modify-write).
